blocks.content: The http-methods topic covered how a typical REST API works, and the grpc-basics topic just introduced a genuinely different approach. This topic is a direct, practical comparison, and a real decision guide for actually choosing between them when building something new.

Neither one is simply, objectively better than the other. They make genuinely different tradeoffs, and a good engineer picks based on the actual, specific situation, not out of habit or whichever one happens to be more familiar.

1. A Direct, Side by Side Comparison
blocks.text: 1. A Direct, Side by Side Comparison

blocks.content: Comparing REST and gRPC across the dimensions that actually matter in practice makes the real tradeoff concrete: data format, how strictly a contract is enforced, how well each one works directly in a browser, and how easily a human can read the raw data itself.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873408-280226402.png
blocks.alt: A Direct, Side by Side Comparison

2. Data Format, Revisited Directly

REST commonly exchanges data as JSON, genuinely readable text a person can look at directly and understand immediately. gRPC uses Protocol Buffers, a compact binary format that is meaningfully smaller and faster to process, but is not something a human can just glance at and read without proper tooling.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873847-278190056.png
3. Browser Support: A Real, Practical Difference
blocks.text: 3. Browser Support: A Real, Practical Difference

blocks.content: A typical REST API works naturally in any web browser, and with virtually any basic HTTP client, no special tooling required at all. gRPC genuinely needs real extra tooling to be used directly from a standard browser, a genuine, practical limitation worth being honest about.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873847-542202179.png
blocks.alt: Browser Support: A Real, Practical Difference

blocks.title: Why this matters so much for public APIs
blocks.content: If external developers, with all kinds of different tools and environments, need to call an API easily, REST genuinely broad, frictionless compatibility becomes a real, practical advantage that is hard to overlook.
4. Human Readability: A Real Debugging Tradeoff
blocks.text: 4. Human Readability: A Real Debugging Tradeoff

blocks.content: A REST response can typically be read directly, glanced at in a browser developer tool, or inspected by eye without any special setup, genuinely convenient for quick debugging. A gRPC response, being binary, needs proper tooling just to actually read what it contains, a real, honest cost when debugging quickly matters.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873848-671926663.png
blocks.alt: Human Readability: A Real Debugging Tradeoff

blocks.content: 5. Performance: A Real Difference That Matters Mainly at Scale
blocks.text: 5. Performance: A Real Difference That Matters Mainly at Scale

blocks.content: REST carries real, genuine overhead, larger text based payloads, typically less efficient connection reuse, but for most everyday use cases, this overhead is genuinely fine and rarely the actual bottleneck. gRPC is meaningfully faster, and that difference actually matters specifically at real scale, high call volume, internal services calling each other constantly.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873848-408830083.png
blocks.alt: Performance: A Real Difference That Matters Mainly at Scale

blocks.title: Do not optimize prematurely
blocks.content: Choosing gRPC purely for its performance advantage, before actually confirming that performance is a genuine bottleneck, often just adds real complexity without a meaningful practical benefit yet.
6. A Practical Decision Guide

For a public facing API meant for external developers, REST is generally the more practical choice, its broad compatibility and readability genuinely matter more than raw performance in this context. For internal, high volume service to service calls, gRPC is generally the stronger fit. For anything genuinely needing real bidirectional streaming, gRPC native support makes it the clear, natural choice.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873848-458002412.png

7. A Common Real World Pattern: Using Both Together
blocks.text: 7. A Common Real World Pattern: Using Both Together

blocks.content: A real company system very often genuinely uses both at once, deliberately, not as an inconsistency. A public facing API exposed to external developers is built with REST, for its broad accessibility, while the internal services behind that same API, talking constantly to each other, communicate over gRPC, for its real speed advantage where it actually matters most.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437873849-357838902.png
blocks.alt: A Common Real World Pattern: Using Both Together

items: Treating this as if one option is simply, objectively superior to the other, when they make genuinely different tradeoffs suited to genuinely different situations.
Choosing gRPC for a public facing API without weighing its real, honest browser support and readability limitations.
Choosing REST for extremely high volume internal service calls without considering whether gRPC real performance advantage would genuinely matter there.
REST favors broad accessibility and human readability; gRPC favors raw performance and a strict, enforced contract.
Using both together, REST externally and gRPC internally, is a genuinely common, deliberate real world pattern, not a compromise.
